name: Search Autocomplete Service
description: Design a search autocomplete system with prefix matching, trie-based caching, and full-text search fallback. Covers prefix indexing, popularity ranking, real-time suggestion serving, and index refresh from the primary database.

learnSteps.title: Trie-Based Prefix Matching
learnSteps.description: The Redis cache stores a trie (prefix tree) as sorted sets: each prefix key maps to a set of completions ranked by popularity score. For query 'sys', Redis returns ZREVRANGE for key 'prefix:sys' yielding ['system design', 'systems programming', 'syslog']. This achieves O(1) Redis lookup + O(K) for top-K results, keeping p99 latency under 5ms. Short prefixes (1-2 chars) are sharded across multiple Redis keys to avoid hot-key issues.

learnSteps.title: Elasticsearch Fallback for Long-Tail Queries
learnSteps.description: When the trie cache misses (rare or long prefixes with <8% miss rate), the service falls back to Elasticsearch using a completion suggester or prefix query. Elasticsearch uses an FST (finite state transducer) index optimized for prefix lookups that returns results in 10-20ms. Results from ES are written back to the Redis trie cache for future requests. This two-tier approach balances speed (Redis for popular) and coverage (ES for long-tail).

learnSteps.title: Popularity Ranking and Freshness
learnSteps.description: Each suggestion has a popularity score derived from search frequency, recency, and trending signals. A batch job runs hourly: it queries PostgreSQL for updated search frequency counts, computes new scores (frequency * recency_decay * trending_boost), and rebuilds the Redis sorted sets. Trending topics get a temporary multiplier that decays over hours. The result is that autocomplete reflects what people are searching for right now, not just historically.

learnSteps.title: Client-Side Optimizations
learnSteps.description: The client implements three key optimizations: (1) Debouncing -- only send a request after 100-150ms of no typing, reducing requests by ~80%. (2) Local caching -- store recent prefix-to-suggestions mappings in a browser/app LRU cache, serving instant results for backspace/retype scenarios. (3) Prefetching -- after receiving results for 'sys', preemptively fetch 'syst' since the user is likely still typing. Combined, these cut server load by 90% while maintaining sub-50ms perceived latency.

chaosScenarios.name: Trie Cache Flush
chaosScenarios.description: Redis loses the prefix index — failover without persistence or an accidental FLUSHALL
chaosScenarios.expectedBehavior: The 92% hit rate drops to zero and 100k RPS of suggestion traffic falls through to Elasticsearch, which can serve only a fraction of it. Suggestion latency jumps from ~5ms to 100ms+, then times out. Correct behavior is silent degradation: clients show no suggestions while search itself stays unaffected.
mitigationSteps: Fail open — return empty suggestion lists on timeout rather than erroring the search box
Rate-limit fallback traffic into Elasticsearch to protect full-text search
Rebuild the trie from the latest hourly score snapshot (bulk ZADD)
Rewarm the highest-volume prefixes first — the head of the query distribution covers most traffic

chaosScenarios.name: Trending-Event Hot Prefix
chaosScenarios.description: Breaking news drives a large share of all queries through a handful of prefixes on one Redis shard
chaosScenarios.expectedBehavior: The shard owning the hot keys saturates its single-threaded CPU; p99 spikes for those prefixes while others stay fast — a partial brownout that aggregate dashboards can miss.
mitigationSteps: Serve hot prefixes from a per-instance in-process LRU on the autocomplete service
Replicate hot keys across N shards and randomize reads
Verify client debouncing and prefix-result reuse are blunting per-keystroke load
Pre-warm predicted follow-on prefixes when the trending pipeline flags a spike

chaosScenarios.name: Elasticsearch Node Loss
chaosScenarios.description: A data node drops out of the cluster configured with 10 shards and 1 replica
chaosScenarios.expectedBehavior: The cluster goes yellow; some shards run without redundancy while reallocation proceeds. Long-tail (cache-miss) suggestions — roughly 8% of traffic — slow or fail for affected shards. Cached head queries are unaffected.
mitigationSteps: Confirm shard reallocation is progressing; throttle recovery if it competes with serving
Serve cache-only (skip the ES fallback) if the cluster goes red
Backfill missed trie write-backs after recovery
Consider replicas: 2 if node loss makes yellow states routine

bottleneckProgression.description: The 10-instance fleet saturates under per-keystroke request rates; queueing pushes p99 past the perceptible threshold
bottleneckProgression.resolution: Scale horizontally — the service is stateless — and confirm client debouncing (100-150ms) is deployed to cut request volume

bottleneckProgression.description: Single-threaded Redis shards bottleneck on ZREVRANGE for popular prefixes
bottleneckProgression.resolution: Add cluster shards and read replicas; cache the head of the prefix distribution in-process on the service tier

bottleneckProgression.description: Even an 8% miss rate exceeds the comfortable Elasticsearch QPS; fallback queries queue behind index refreshes
bottleneckProgression.resolution: Raise the cache hit rate first (more memory, longer TTL) before adding ES data nodes

expectedIssues.title: Hot Short Prefixes
expectedIssues.description: One- and two-character prefixes concentrate a huge share of lookups onto few keys, defeating uniform sharding
expectedIssues.mitigation: Shard short prefixes across multiple keys (as designed) and add in-process caching for the head of the distribution

expectedIssues.title: Trending Lag from Hourly Rebuilds
expectedIssues.description: Popularity scores refresh hourly, so suggestions trail breaking events by up to 60 minutes
expectedIssues.mitigation: Layer a lightweight streaming bump for query counts on top of the hourly full rebuild; apply trending multipliers out-of-band

expectedIssues.title: Cold-Cache Stampede
expectedIssues.description: After a flush or failover, simultaneous misses stampede Elasticsearch with lookups and write-backs
expectedIssues.mitigation: Singleflight per prefix, bounded ES fallback concurrency, and a bulk rewarm job instead of organic refill

expectedIssues.title: Suggestion Poisoning
expectedIssues.description: Coordinated query spam can push offensive or manipulative completions into the popularity index
expectedIssues.mitigation: Denylist filtering at rebuild time, per-IP/user query frequency caps, and anomaly detection on sudden score jumps

expectedIssues.title: Thin Elasticsearch Redundancy
expectedIssues.description: With replicas: 1, any single data-node loss removes redundancy for the shards it hosted
expectedIssues.mitigation: Raise the replica count or ensure fast automated node replacement

slaDefinitions.name: Suggestion Latency
slaDefinitions.penalty: Internal SLO — suggestions slower than ~100ms are dropped client-side and worthless mid-typing

slaDefinitions.name: Availability (Fail-Open)
slaDefinitions.penalty: Internal SLO — outages degrade to empty suggestions, never block search

slaDefinitions.name: Index Freshness
slaDefinitions.penalty: Stale-index review with the search quality team

metrics.name: empty_response_rate
metrics.description: Share of requests returning no suggestions (fail-open indicator)

metrics.name: index_refresh_age_minutes
metrics.description: Time since the last successful score rebuild

dashboards: Suggest Serving (latency, hit rate, empty rate)

steps: Confirm fail-open behavior — the search box should degrade, not error
Cap ES fallback concurrency to protect full-text search
Kick off the bulk rewarm from the latest score snapshot
Watch hit rate recover; prioritize head prefixes
Identify hot keys (redis-cli --hotkeys, latency by prefix)
Enable in-process caching for the affected prefixes
Pre-warm the follow-on prefixes the event will generate next
Check the hourly rebuild job logs and PostgreSQL query health
Re-run the rebuild manually and verify score updates land in Redis
If prolonged, notify search quality about trending lag

decisions.title: Two-Tier Lookup: Redis Trie + Elasticsearch Fallback
decisions.context: Head queries need single-digit-millisecond responses per keystroke; long-tail prefixes need coverage without holding everything in RAM
decisions.decision: Precomputed prefix-to-completions sorted sets in Redis serve ~92% of traffic; the ES completion suggester handles misses, with results written back to the cache
consequences: p99 stays around 5ms for the vast majority of lookups
Long-tail prefixes still answer in 10-20ms via ES
Two systems must stay consistent through the write-back and rebuild paths

decisions.title: Hourly Batch Scoring from the Primary DB
decisions.context: Popularity ranking blends frequency, recency decay, and trending boosts
decisions.decision: An hourly job recomputes scores from PostgreSQL and rebuilds the Redis sorted sets
consequences: A simple, restartable pipeline with one source of truth
Trending suggestions lag real events by up to an hour
Rebuilds create predictable bursts of Redis write load

decisions.title: Fail-Open Degradation
decisions.context: Autocomplete is an enhancement; the search box must never break because suggestions are down
decisions.decision: Timeouts return empty suggestion lists; clients render nothing and search proceeds normally
consequences: Cache or ES outages become UX degradations, not user-facing outages
Failures can go unnoticed without empty-response-rate monitoring
The availability target can be 99.9% instead of 99.99%, saving redundancy cost

tradeoffs.benefit: O(1) lookups with no scoring work at read time
tradeoffs.cost: Suggestions trail real-world trends by up to an hour

tradeoffs.choice: Cache only the head of the query distribution (64GB)
tradeoffs.benefit: An order of magnitude cheaper than holding the full corpus in RAM
tradeoffs.cost: Roughly 8% of lookups pay the ES fallback latency
Cannot reflect breaking events within minutes

alternatives.name: Pure Elasticsearch Completion Suggester
alternatives.description: Serve all suggestions from the FST-based ES suggester with no Redis tier
alternatives.prosVsCons: One system and good relevance tooling, but a 10-20ms baseline plus JVM GC tails make per-keystroke p99 at 100k RPS expensive
alternatives.whyNotChosen: Redis head caching cuts both latency and the required ES fleet size dramatically

alternatives.name: In-Process Tries on Service Nodes
alternatives.description: Ship the full trie inside each autocomplete instance
alternatives.prosVsCons: The fastest possible lookups with no network hop, but every node holds the full index and rebuilds require coordinated rollouts
alternatives.whyNotChosen: Centralized Redis simplifies refresh and keeps service instances stateless and cheap to scale

alternatives.name: Streaming Popularity Updates (Kafka + Flink)
alternatives.description: Update scores continuously from the live query log stream
alternatives.prosVsCons: Minutes-fresh trending, but adds a stream-processing platform for a feature where hourly freshness is mostly acceptable
alternatives.whyNotChosen: Deferred until product data shows trending lag materially hurts engagement
